# Disagreement Log — T12_010 (Testament of Asher)
**Chapter:** T12_010 | **Verses:** 7 sections (~8 verses)
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA

| # | Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA ruling |
|---|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 1:3 | Key terms "two ways" | "two-ways, two-minds, two-kinds-of-action, two-modes, two-issues" | "two ways, two inclinations, two kinds of action, two modes, two issues" | "Two ways. Two inclinations. Two kinds of action. Two outcomes." | LOGOS phrasing adopted; "inclinations" better than "minds" for Greek dianoia in ethical context |
| 2 | 3:2 | "Two faces" | "men-of-two-faces" | "men who have double faces" | "double-faced people" | "men of two faces" — EMET/LOGOS; prosōpon dittou is the technical term and should be preserved literally |
| 3 | 5:1 | Stag/hind comparison | "stags-and-hinds" | "stags and hinds" | "stags and deer" | "stags and hinds" — EMET/LOGOS; elaphoi kai dorcades is gender-paired in the Greek; PNEUMA loses the pairing |
| 4 | 6:4–5 | Wisdom-in-exile passage | Full passage | Full passage | Full passage | All three agree; SOPHIA preserves "in a strange country a fatherland" — one of the most beautiful lines in the Testaments |
| 5 | 7:1 | "Enthroned with kings" | Not present in EMET section 7 | Present: "Whosoever teacheth these things...shall be enthroned with kings, as was Joseph our brother" | Present: "will be enthroned among kings — as Joseph was" | SOPHIA includes — the Joseph reference appears in the MS and is confirmed by LOGOS and PNEUMA |

---
*SOPHIA notes: Testament of Asher presents the most developed philosophical framework in the corpus — a binary moral ontology (two inclinations, two faces) that anticipates Qumran's Two Spirits teaching (1QS III–IV). The key distinction between "single-faced" and "double-faced" persons is not about hypocrisy alone, but about the fundamental orientation of the soul. The "stags and hinds" comparison is a levitical purity allusion. SOPHIA notes that the "enthroned with kings, as was Joseph" line appears in LOGOS and PNEUMA but not in EMET — this is a scribal discrepancy; it is included as it appears to be authentic.*
